title: Reporting Div 296 earnings favourable
full_text:
A senior chartered accounting executive has suggested it is in the interest of SMSF trustees to report any Division 296 tax earnings on the annual return for members they know will be captured by the measure, which is in line with the ATO’s expectation.
“The expectation from the tax office is that almost every fund, where it is known that a [member] is in scope, needs to declare that Division 296 earnings figure in the SMSF annual return, [even though] we don’t know what that looks like yet,” Cooper Partners director and head of SMSF and succession Jemma Sanderson told delegates at The Tax Institute National Superannuation Conference hosted in Melbourne a few weeks ago.
Sanderson took the opportunity to point out following this reporting discipline will ultimately be in the interest of trustees as it will prevent additional corrective administration actions.
“If you don’t declare that figure and then you lodge the return, and then the tax office comes back and says: ‘oh, Jemma, you’ve lodged this return for the Jemma Super Fund, we need the Division 296 [earnings] figure [we didn’t receive],’ and then you have to go and look at the work papers and get an actuarial certificate subsequent to that,” she explained.
“The other thing that it is looking like, [according to] the tax office’s current draft guidelines online, is that to amend that [earnings] figure [will be] an amendment to the SMSF annual return [and] that’s the last thing we want to be doing.
“So we want to make it as simple as possible.”
According to Sanderson, the sector expectation is for the administration software providers to provide a feature to automate the Division 296 reporting process.
“That will have a separate column [to accommodate] the Division 296 [capital gains tax (CGT)] cost base, if you’ve [elected to adjust the CGT assets], and then hopefully it will be able to calculate what the amounts are,” she said.
“[Then] the actuary [will] give you the figures, you disclose them in the return, and then you’ve done that bit and you don’t need to then consider [amending the SMSF annual] return later.”
author: Darin Tyson-Chan
